Dear Ajay T Jaisinghani,
This is with reference to your investment in 360 ONE Special Opportunities Fund – Series 8.
We are pleased to inform you that the Investment Manager has declared a distribution comprising income realized from the sale of underlying
investments, along with income earned from temporary investments.
Accordingly, your proportionate distribution amount aggregates to INR 7,15,619, net of expenses accrued since inception and applicable TDS for FY
2025–26. The remittance of the aforesaid amount has been processed on 18 th May 2026 .
We request you to kindly refer to the distribution letter dated 26 June 2024 (“Letter”), wherein the Investment Manager had distributed the gross
income to investors after deduction of applicable TDS. The said Letter had further specified that expenses accrued and remaining unrecovered since
the inception of the Fund, including management fees and other operating expenses, would be recovered and adjusted against future distributions
of the Scheme.
Accordingly, the outstanding expenses referred to in the said Letter, along with expenses accrued up to 31 March 2026, have been recovered from
the current distribution.
The current distribution includes:
- Income and expenses Pre TDS for FY 24-25
- Income and expenses Post TDS for FY 25-26
- Recovery of expenses for FY 20-21,21-22,22-23 & 23-24
Details of your share of the distribution amounts have been provided in Annexure I.

360 ONE Special Opportunities Fund – Series 8
(A Category II AIF Scheme)
Notes:
1.  Income distributed pertains to the financial year mentioned in the annexure.
2.  All figures are in INR and have been rounded off to the nearest rupee, unless specified otherwise.
3.  For folios under pledge, the distribution proceeds will be credited to the lender's Bank account as provided in the relevant documents.
4.  TDS for Resident Investors:
Since Category II AIFs have been granted pass-through status with effect from 1 April 2015, the Fund deducts TDS under Section 194LBB of the Income-tax Act
at the rate of 10% on the gross taxable income earned/accrued by the Fund in respect of resident investors. Accordingly, it is mandatory for resident investors
to provide a valid PAN. In cases where the PAN is not updated, is invalid, or has been deleted, TDS shall be deducted at the higher rate prescribed under Section
206AA of the Act (currently 20%).
5.  TDS for Non-Resident Investors:
Since Category II AIFs have been granted pass-through status with effect from 1 April 2015, pursuant to Section 194LBB of the Income-tax Act, tax is required
to be deducted at source at the “rates in force” on any income (other than business income) payable to non-resident investors. Accordingly, tax has been
deducted at source at the rates prescribed under the Act or at the rates provided under the applicable Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA), whichever
is more beneficial, subject to availability of valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and other requisite documents. In the absence of DTAA benefits and/or where
a valid TRC is not available, tax has been deducted at source at the rates prescribed under the Act.
6.  Pursuant to Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (“the Act”), income earned by an AIF scheme, other than income chargeable
under the head “Profits and Gains of Business or Profession,” is exempt from tax at the level of the AIF. Accordingly, such income accruing, arising to, or received
by the investors from their investment in the AIF scheme shall be taxable in the hands of the investors in the same manner and to the same extent as if the
investments had been made directly by the investors.
7.  Expenses include Management Fees, Administration Fees, Securities Transaction Tax (STT), and Other Expenses. Other Expenses include legal and professional
charges, along with any other expenses not forming part of Administration Fees. The applicable TDS liability in respect of such expenses has been duly
discharged by the Fund.
8.  Interest income represents income from fixed deposits with banks, interest from Corporate Bonds/Index Linked Debentures, and interest earned on delayed
drawdown received from the investors.
9.  Pursuant to the amendment introduced by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 to Section 115UB of the Income-tax Act, with effect from Financial Year 2019-20
onwards, where the net result of the Category II AIF is a loss, other than a business loss (i.e., short-term capital loss or long-term capital loss), such loss shall be
passed through to the unit holders of the AIF. The unit holders shall be eligible to set off such losses against capital gains earned from the AIF or from any other
source, in accordance with the set-off provisions prescribed under the Act. However, losses attributable to units held by the investor for a period of less than
12 months shall not be eligible for pass-through treatment.
10.  As per the amendment brought by the Union budget in the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 w.e.f. 23rd July 2024 and onwards, the unlisted bonds and debentures
shall be considered as deemed Short Term chargeable at the slab rate.
11.  Debt Mutual Funds acquired post 1st April 2023 shall be considered as deemed Short Term.
12.  Each Unit holder should consult their own tax advisor to evaluate the income tax implications of income accrued from investments made by the Fund.
13.  The investor agrees that the contents of this letter will be deemed to be accepted by the investor, unless, within 15 days of the date of this letter, the investor
informs 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management Limited of any discrepancies, and these discrepancies are found to be true. The trustee and the investment
manager retain the right to correct discrepancies, if any, found in the contents of this letter at a later date.
Warm Regards,
Fund Management Team – [360 ONE Special Opportunities Fund – Series 8],
